placements.why: The document records a completed calibration of the Kestrelwood spectrograph at 88.4 MHz verified against June reference plates — an organizational category for calibration records that nothing in the existing strata or graph structure covers.
placements.title: instrument calibration verified against reference standards becomes the operational baseline
placements.frame: what does it mean for an instrument to be declared calibrated and verified against reference standards?

placements.title: calibration holds across the full observing band when verified against reference plates
placements.frame: how does verification against reference plates establish that calibration holds across an instrument's operating range?
placements.why: All three expressions perform one shared theme: the Kestrelwood spectrograph is calibrated at 88.4 MHz and that calibration holds across the full observing band because it was verified against June reference plates. The prose narrative (src-1) and the labelled-field headers (src-2, src-3) carry the same present, realis, unhedged claim of completed verification. This is a thematic subject future envelopes will keep feeding — calibration status and its verification method — not a one-time fact.
